title: Why Most People Don't Know About the Presale Game
seoTitle: Why Most People Don't Know About the Presale Game
description: The presale game works like a club: insiders get the new projects first. How to get on the list, and how to tell an overextended market from an opportunity.
answer: The presale game is a club. Once you are on brokers' and developers' lists, new projects come to you first and you have leverage. Outsiders must search for deals. The next skill is reading markets: avoid overextended ones where presale prices already exceed finished homes.
body:
Why don't more people know about buying presales? Because it works like a club.

## Being inside the club

When you are part of it, brokers and developers keep you on their radar. Their newsletters about the next launch reach you before the public hears about it. When they are looking for you, you have the leverage. When you have to go looking for them, they have it.

So the first part of the game is simple: get on as many lists as possible, with brokers and developers working on new developments, in your city and beyond.

## Home markets and foreign markets

When you play in your own country, you know the rules and the law protects you. Playing abroad carries more risk. But some foreign markets also offer much more room for profit, because the gap between presale prices and finished prices is still wide.

## Overextended and underextended markets

The presale game does not work the same way everywhere.

- **Underextended markets** still have room to grow. Presale prices are below comparable finished homes, so early buyers can capture the gap.
- **Overextended markets** have used up that room. Profits from the past are no longer guaranteed, and a correction may be coming.

## The warning sign

When presale units are priced higher than existing properties of similar quality nearby, the market is likely overextended. Dubai today reminds me of Toronto four or five years ago, when many people believed they could assign any contract for an easy profit. Keep an eye on markets like that: the risk is high, and your profit can disappear.
takeaways: Presale access works like a club: insiders hear about projects first.
When developers come to you, you have the leverage.
Your home market gives legal protection; foreign markets can offer bigger gaps.
Presale prices above comparable finished homes signal an overextended market.
faq: How do I get access to presale projects early?
Register with brokers who specialize in new developments and sign up directly with developers in the markets you follow, so launch information reaches you first.
What is an overextended real estate market?
A market where presale prices already match or exceed the prices of comparable finished homes, leaving little profit for early buyers.
Is it safe to buy off-plan in another country?
It carries extra risk because you may not know the rules or have the same legal protection, so research the local laws and the developer carefully.
